native_scope: Original fixed KR build, original bindings, valid thread/owner, available capacity, no reentrant/debug/GC hook interference
core_claim: An ordinary Lua error escaping the inner body can return false,error to the still-running outer, making effect-aware cleanup selection reachable without wrapping a yielding entry in same-thread pcall.
old_R9_statement_refinement: Direct entry-call cleanup after a raised error was not reachable. The additional protected child resume supplies a new caller path; external cancellation and outer failures remain uncovered.

scheduling.inner_context_delivery: Lua adapter captures RUN_CONTEXT and calls entry(RUN_CONTEXT)
scheduling.child_yield_values_if_present: Ignored; never interpreted as sleep or forwarded as future arguments

native_thread_fields.owner: lua_State only; not Q manager offsets

inner_constraints: Finite work between cooperative yields; no scheduler reentry or duplicate registration
No direct Register/qco-list mutation, no End/Stop/removeAll/remove of outer
No surviving/external child handle references or later resume after cleanup
No mutation of shared original coroutine/MoCo/qbase/Q/helper bindings
Own export and shared context only; record actual partial effects for selected cleanup
No dependence on coroutine.running() being the scheduler-registered outer
Bounded zero-value yield and at most one result payload; native API supports more but this adapter does not proxy them

cancellation.cooperative_flag: Design-owned local context flag with a concrete producer still to be assigned; not a new native/Server API

cleanup.owner: outer supervisor and a separately validated effect policy
